data.long_meaning: The one who possesses knowledge and wisdom. in_arabic.name: حنبل
in_arabic.long_meaning: حنبل: اسم علم男性 عربي، مشتق من الحنابلة التي كانت فروع من المذهب الشافعي. يُعتبر الشخص الذي يتبع المذهب الحنابي. من أهم المراجع عند الحنابلة: الإمام أحمد بن حنبل. يُشار إلى الحنابلة بالمرجع، والمعتمد، والعائد إلى الحنابلة. في التسمية، يُعتبر الحنبل من أشهر الأسماء في المذهب الشافعي، ويُقترن عادةً مع الألقاب التي تعكس الروح الحنابية، مثل: الحنبلية، الحنابلة، الحنابية. يُعتبر الحنبل من أهم الأسماء التي يُمارس فيها المذهب الحنابي، ويُعتبر مصدر إلهام للشخصيات المُعتبرة في المذهب الحنابي.

in_hindi.name: हनबल
in_hindi.long_meaning: हनबल: यह एक पारसी नाम है जो हनाब्ली के नाम का रूपांतरण है। इसका अर्थ मूल्य, सहारा और हनाब्ली है। यह नाम हनाब्ली संप्रदाय के अनुयायियों के लिए विशिष्ट है। इसका संबंध इमाम अहमद बिन हनबल से है, जो हनाब्ली संप्रदाय के एक प्रमुख प्रवर्तक थे। हनबल नाम हनाब्ली संप्रदाय के अनुयायियों में एक प्रसिद्ध नाम है। यह नाम हनाब्ली परंपरा का प्रतिनिधि है और हनाब्ली संप्रदाय की आत्मा को दर्शाता है।

in_pashto.name: حنبل
in_pashto.long_meaning: حنبل: د یوځې عربی نوم دی چې له حنابليۍ څخه اخیستل شوی دی. دا یو نوم دی چې معنی یې مرجع، مُعتمد او حنبليۍ وي. دا نوم حنبليۍ فرقې ته اړوند دی. دا نوم د امام احمد بن حنبل سره اړوند دی چې یو له دغه فرقې لومړنیو پیروکارانو څخه وو. دا نوم یو پخوانی نوم دی چې د حنبليۍ فرقې له مخې جوړ شوی دی. دا نوم د دغه فرقې د رواج څخه ډیری مشهور دی.

data.cultural_impact: The name Hanbal carries a rich history and cultural significance in the Islamic world. It is derived from the famous Islamic Scholar Imam Ahmad bin Hanbal (855-855 CE), who was a prominent figure in the development of the Hanbali School of Islamic Jurisprudence. Imam Ahmad bin Hanbal is remembered for his unwavering commitment to traditional Sunan Sahih (authentic Prophetic traditions) and his steadfast rejection of Bid'ah (innovations) in Islamic practice. His name Hanbal came to represent a strong adherence to the classical Islamic religious teachings and became synonymous with a conservative and purist approach to Islamic law and theology. In the Hindu Kush region of Central Asia, the name Hanbal is sometimes used as an honorific or title for scholars and religious figures, reflecting a continued respect for the legacy of Imam Ahmad bin Hanbal and his contributions to Islamic scholarship. (The name Hanbal is also commonly used in Western countries in the context of the "Hanbali branch of Islamic Thought" or "Hanbali Fiqh" - Islamic law).
data.spiritual_significance: The name Hanbal holds a deep spiritual significance in the Islamic world. It signifies a strong believer in Allah, who strives to seek knowledge and wisdom from the Divine Revelation. The name is a reminder of the importance of adhering to the Prophetic traditions and the Quran in one's religious practice. It is a symbol of the commitment to preserve the authentic teachings of Islam and reject any deviation from the true path. The name Hanbal inspires one to be a custodian of Islamic knowledge and wisdom, and to strive towards becoming a scholar and a righteous example to others in one's community. It engenders a sense of humility, reverence, and dedication towards Allah, the Source of all knowledge and wisdom. The name Hanbal is a source of inspiration and pride, reminding the bearer of the noble legacy of Imam Ahmad bin Hanbal and the priceless contributions he made to the Islamic world.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Hanbal is derived from the Arabic word "Hanbalah," meaning "preserving the Prophet's tradition." Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, the eponym of this scholarly tradition, was known for his unwavering commitment to preserving the Prophet Muhammad's teachings and practices.

islamic_reference.note: Traditional Islamic name with deep spiritual significance in Islamic culture

historical_references.reference: Ibn Abd al-Hadid (1211-1258 CE) in his book ‘Sharh Nahj al-Balaghah’ wrote about Ibn Hanbal and his Hanbali school of thought, which became prominent in the 9th century CE.
historical_references.context: Rise of the Hanbali School of Thought

historical_references.reference: Ibn Khaldun (1332-1406 CE) in his ‘Muqaddimah’ described Ibn Hanbal as a noted scholar in Hadith and Fiqh. He also mentioned that Ibn Hanbal’s followers rejected the rationalist and philosophical trends that dominated the Islamic world during the Abbasid Caliphate.
historical_references.context: Rejection of Rationalist and Philosophical Trends
